A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original polynomial regression, physical-system prediction, top-quark tagging, noise-robustness, and symmetry-recovery results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 8–10 add representation procedures using general invertible coordinate transformations and hyperbolic or shear canonicalization, extending v1's rotational construction. These are substantive proposed feature-map adaptations; the original network training procedure remains unchanged, and implementation of the extensions is not reported.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same polynomial functions, anisotropic quantum system, double pendulum, moment-of-inertia prediction, and top-quark tagging. The new SL(n) constructions introduce no evaluated datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: LieGAN and Augerino in the retained comparisons, EMLP in the physical tasks, and LieGG in Appendix B.2/Table B.5. No additional comparator is experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation metrics, 100-epoch Adam training with learning rate 0.001, model configurations, noise levels, and reference-matrix comparison settings are unchanged. The added theory introduces no experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same noise tests on u(x) and r(x). The interpretability analyses and matrix visualizations in Appendix B.5/Figures 4–5 are also unchanged; Appendix C adds proofs rather than empirical analyses.

E5.justification: The three-independent-seed disclosure and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. Table B.5 still distinguishes aggregated polynomial results from single-run double-pendulum results. Removing the checklist does not remove the underlying statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 5.1–5.2, 6.1, and B.2–B.5 and the empirical figures match. Section 6.3 retains 88.03% top-quark accuracy and the same 89.96% comparison value. No new empirical findings accompany the theoretical extension.

T1.justification: New Sections 7–11 introduce SL(n) generator classifications, three canonical representation definitions, generalized orbit representation/separation propositions, and an invariant-function factorization theorem. New Appendix C supplies elliptic-case proofs and asserts analogous proofs for hyperbolic and parabolic cases. The original theory is retained.

C1.justification: The new Sections 7–11 claim representation and factorization guarantees beyond rotations, covering elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic SL(n) subgroups. Table 6.2 correspondingly changes the advertised scope from SO(n) to SL(n). However, the abstract, original contribution bullets, and conclusion retain their SO(n)-focused claims.

C2.justification: The extension adds geometric interpretations of bounded rotational versus unbounded squeeze/shear orbits and explains canonicalization across these cases. Existing empirical interpretations and the concluding limitations concerning tensors and broader Lie groups remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Removing the checklist removes statements that supplementary material contains a code ZIP and asset instructions. Architecture, optimizer, hardware, and the implementation link in Appendix B remain unchanged. This is a disclosure change, not evidence that resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: Table 6.2 broadens the method's advertised symmetry scope relative to the same comparison methods. The related-work discussion and cited-work membership remain unchanged; reference-name typography edits introduce no new literature.

P1.justification: Existing prose is largely verbatim. Structural edits insert the extension before the conclusion, append Appendix C, and remove the checklist. v2 also adds conference text and an unedited acknowledgments template. Most additional text documents new theory rather than rewriting the original narrative.

P2.justification: The existing figures and table structures are retained. Figure 1 shifts with text reflow, while Figure 5 moves from a standalone page to one shared with Appendix C proof text. Conference/footer additions and the inserted sections alter local pagination without redesigning the displays.

improvement.justification: The added SL(n) generalization substantially weakens theoretical reliability. For A=I, λ1=1, and v1=(1,2), Definition 9.1 requires tanh(t0)=2, so the claimed representative does not exist. In the two-dimensional shear case, Definition 10.1 cannot separate distinct fixed points (a,0), contradicting Section 11's universal orbit guarantees. Appendix C's asserted transfer of elliptic proofs does not resolve these failures. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, while the newly advertised scope rests on invalid general guarantees.
